column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|03-15|1767|Άντριου Τζάκσον|Andrew Jackson|Andrew Jackson was the 7th president of the United States, from 1829 to 1837. He was a general and a hero of the Battle of New Orleans, and the first president to come from the common people. He supported the removal of Native Americans from their lands.

bio|03-15|1830|Πάουλ Γιόχαν Λούντβιχ φον Χάιζε|Paul von Heyse|Paul von Heyse was a German writer of novellas, poet and translator. He was very well regarded in his time, and in 1910 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-15|1854|Έμιλ φον Μπέρινγκ|Emil von Behring|Emil von Behring was a German doctor and microbiologist. He developed the serum against diphtheria and tetanus, and in 1901 he became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.

bio|03-15|1937|Χάουαρντ Φίλιπς Λάβκραφτ|Howard Phillips Lovecraft|H. P. Lovecraft was an American writer of horror and science fiction stories. He created the "Cthulhu Mythos". He lived in poverty and was recognised only after his death.

bio|03-15|1938|Νικολάι Μπουχάριν|Nikolai Bukharin|Nikolai Bukharin was a Russian Bolshevik politician and theorist. He supported the New Economic Policy. He was executed in 1938 during the Moscow Trials, on the charge of treason.

bio|03-15|1943|Ντέιβιντ Κρόνενμπεργκ|David Cronenberg|David Cronenberg is a Canadian director and screenwriter. He became known for horror and science fiction films such as "The Fly" and "Videodrome", and later for dramas such as "A History of Violence".

bio|03-15|1962|Άρθουρ Χόλι Κόμπτον|Arthur Holly Compton|Arthur Compton was an American physicist. He discovered that X-rays are scattered by electrons with a change in wavelength, the Compton effect, and in 1927 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.
bio|03-15|1993|Πολ Πογκμπά|Paul Pogba|Paul Pogba is a French footballer. He played for Juventus and Manchester United and won the 2018 World Cup with France.

bio|03-16|37|Τιβέριος Καίσαρας Αύγουστος|Tiberius|Tiberius was the second Roman emperor, from 14 to 37, the successor of Augustus. He was an experienced general. In his last years he lived on Capri, withdrawn from Rome. He died in 37 AD.

bio|03-16|455|Ουαλεντινιανός Γ΄|Valentinian III|Valentinian III was emperor of the Western Roman Empire from 425 to 455. He was incompetent and the empire lost many provinces. He was murdered in 455 by followers of the general Aetius.

bio|03-16|1751|Τζέιμς Μάντισον|James Madison|James Madison was the 4th president of the United States, from 1809 to 1817. He is regarded as the "father of the Constitution" of the United States and, together with others, wrote "The Federalist Papers".

bio|03-16|1789|Γκέοργκ Ωμ|Georg Ohm|Georg Ohm was a German physicist. He formulated Ohm's law on the relation between voltage, current and resistance in electrical circuits. The unit of electrical resistance, the ohm, is named after him.

bio|03-16|1839|Συλί Προυντόμ|Sully Prudhomme|Sully Prudhomme was a French poet. He was a member of the Parnassian movement, and in 1901 he became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-16|1930|Μιγκέλ Πρίμο ντε Ριβέρα|Miguel Primo de Rivera|Miguel Primo de Rivera was a Spanish general. He seized power in a coup in 1923 and ruled as a dictator until 1930. He was the father of the founder of the Falange, Jose Antonio.

bio|03-16|1940|Σέλμα Λάγκερλεφ|Selma Lagerlof|Selma Lagerlof was a Swedish writer. She wrote the children's book "The Wonderful Adventures of Nils", and in 1909 she became the first woman to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-16|1953|Ρίτσαρντ Στόλλμαν|Richard Stallman|Richard Stallman is an American programmer and activist. He started the free software movement and in 1983 launched the GNU project. He founded the Free Software Foundation.

bio|03-16|1959|Γενς Στόλτενμπεργκ|Jens Stoltenberg|Jens Stoltenberg is a Norwegian politician. He was prime minister of Norway and from 2014 to 2024 secretary general of NATO. He became finance minister of Norway in 2025.

bio|03-17|180|Μάρκος Αυρήλιος|Marcus Aurelius|Marcus Aurelius was a Roman emperor from 161 to 180 and a Stoic philosopher. He wrote "Meditations", a work in Greek with personal reflections. He died on campaign against the Germanic tribes.

bio|03-17|599|Αλί ιμπν Αμπού Τάλιμπ|Ali ibn Abi Talib|Ali was a cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet Muhammad and the fourth caliph. His era was marked by civil wars and by the division of Muslims into Sunnis and Shias.

bio|03-17|763|Χαρούν αλ Ρασίντ|Harun al-Rashid|Harun al-Rashid was the fifth Abbasid caliph, from 786 to 809. Baghdad under his rule was a centre of culture. He appears in "The Thousand and One Nights".

bio|03-17|1537|Τογιοτόμι Χιντεγιόσι|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Toyotomi Hideyoshi was a Japanese warlord. He unified Japan after decades of civil war and ruled from 1585 to 1598. He attempted to invade Korea.

bio|03-17|1680|Φρανσουά ντε Λα Ροσφουκώ|Francois de La Rochefoucauld|Francois de La Rochefoucauld was a French writer. He wrote the "Maxims", short and cynical reflections on human nature. He also took part in the Fronde uprising.

bio|03-17|1834|Γκότλιμπ Ντάιμλερ|Gottlieb Daimler|Gottlieb Daimler was a German engineer and inventor. He developed the first fast petrol engine and built a motorcycle and a car. He founded Daimler-Motoren-Gesellschaft, which later became Mercedes-Benz.

bio|03-17|1919|Νατ Κινγκ Κόουλ|Nat King Cole|Nat King Cole was an American jazz singer and pianist. He started with a trio and became very popular as a singer, with hits such as "Unforgettable" and "Mona Lisa".

bio|03-17|1956|Ιρέν Ζολιό-Κιουρί|Irene Joliot-Curie|Irene Joliot-Curie was a French chemist and the daughter of Marie and Pierre Curie. With her husband Frederic she discovered artificial radioactivity, and in 1935 they shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

bio|03-17|2017|Ντέρεκ Γουόλκοτ|Derek Walcott|Derek Walcott was a poet and playwright from Saint Lucia in the Caribbean. He wrote the epic poem "Omeros", and in 1992 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-18|1768|Λώρενς Στερν|Laurence Sterne|Laurence Sterne was an Irish writer and clergyman. He wrote the experimental novel "The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy" and "A Sentimental Journey". He was important for the development of the novel.

bio|03-18|1837|Γκρόβερ Κλίβελαντ|Grover Cleveland|Grover Cleveland was the 22nd and the 24th president of the United States. He is the only president to have served two non-consecutive terms, from 1885 to 1889 and from 1893 to 1897.

bio|03-18|1844|Νικολάι Ρίμσκι-Κόρσακοφ|Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov|Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov was a Russian composer and a member of "The Five". He wrote "Scheherazade" and "The Flight of the Bumblebee". He was a teacher of Stravinsky and an expert in orchestration.

bio|03-18|1858|Ρούντολφ Ντίζελ|Rudolf Diesel|Rudolf Diesel was a German engineer. He invented the diesel engine, which uses compression to ignite the fuel. He disappeared in 1913 from a ship in the English Channel.

bio|03-18|1869|Νέβιλ Τσάμπερλεν|Neville Chamberlain|Neville Chamberlain was a British Conservative politician and prime minister from 1937 to 1940. He is associated with the policy of appeasement towards Nazi Germany and with the Munich Agreement of 1938.
bio|03-18|1932|Τζον Άπνταϊκ|John Updike|John Updike was an American writer. He wrote the "Rabbit" series of novels about Harry Angstrom, and he twice won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction.

bio|03-18|1980|Έριχ Φρομ|Erich Fromm|Erich Fromm was a German psychologist and philosopher. He lived in the United States and wrote books such as "The Fear of Freedom" and "The Art of Loving", combining psychoanalysis with social criticism.

bio|03-18|2017|Τσακ Μπέρι|Chuck Berry|Chuck Berry was an American guitarist and songwriter and one of the pioneers of rock and roll. He wrote songs such as "Johnny B. Goode" and "Roll Over Beethoven". He influenced many musicians.

bio|03-19|1406|Ιμπν Χαλντούν|Ibn Khaldun|Ibn Khaldun was an Arab historian and sociologist from Tunis. In his work "Muqaddimah" he analysed the rise and decline of societies, and he is regarded as a forerunner of sociology and economics.
bio|03-19|1702|Γουλιέλμος Γ΄|William III|William III of Orange was a Dutch prince and from 1689 king of England, together with his wife Mary II after the "Glorious Revolution". He opposed Louis XIV.

bio|03-19|1813|Ντέιβιντ Λίβινγκστον|David Livingstone|David Livingstone was a Scottish missionary and explorer of Africa. He discovered the Victoria Falls and searched for the sources of the Nile. He became known through his meeting with Stanley in 1871.

bio|03-19|1821|Ρίτσαρντ Μπάρτον|Richard Burton|Richard Burton was a British explorer and writer. He travelled disguised to Mecca and Medina and explored East Africa. He translated "The Thousand and One Nights".

bio|03-19|1906|Άντολφ Άιχμαν|Adolf Eichmann|Adolf Eichmann was an SS officer and one of the organisers of the Holocaust in Nazi Germany. He fled to Argentina and was abducted from there by Israel in 1960. He was tried and executed in 1962.

bio|03-19|1949|Βαλέρι Λεόντιεφ|Valeri Leontiev|Valeri Leontiev is a Russian singer. He became very well known in the Soviet Union and in Russia with songs in a folk and pop style. He has been honoured with the title of People's Artist.

bio|03-19|1955|Μπρους Γουίλις|Bruce Willis|Bruce Willis is an American actor. He became known through the series "Moonlighting" and for the roles of John McClane in "Die Hard", in "Pulp Fiction" and in "The Sixth Sense".

bio|03-19|1987|Λουί ντε Μπρολί|Louis de Broglie|Louis de Broglie was a French physicist. He proposed that particles have a wave nature, and in 1929 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. His idea helped shape quantum mechanics.

bio|03-19|2008|Άρθουρ Κλαρκ|Arthur C. Clarke|Arthur C. Clarke was an English science fiction writer. He wrote "2001: A Space Odyssey" and proposed the use of geostationary satellites for telecommunications. He spent his last years in Sri Lanka.
bio|03-20|1413|Ερρίκος Δ΄|Henry IV|Henry IV was king of England from 1399, when he deposed his cousin Richard II. He faced many rebellions and died in 1413. He was succeeded by his son Henry V.

bio|03-20|1770|Φρήντριχ Χαίλντερλιν|Friedrich Holderlin|Friedrich Holderlin was a German poet. He wrote hymns and odes inspired by ancient Greece and the novel "Hyperion". He suffered from mental illness and spent his last years in a tower in Tubingen.

bio|03-20|1811|Ναπολέων Β΄|Napoleon II|Napoleon II was the son of Napoleon I and Marie Louise. He was proclaimed King of Rome and, after his father's abdication, briefly emperor, but he did not really reign. He died young in Vienna.

bio|03-20|1828|Ερρίκος Ίψεν|Henrik Ibsen|Henrik Ibsen was a Norwegian playwright. He wrote plays such as "A Doll's House", "Ghosts" and "An Enemy of the People". He is regarded as the "father of modern drama".

bio|03-20|1929|Φερντινάν Φος|Ferdinand Foch|Ferdinand Foch was a French marshal. He was the commander-in-chief of the Allied forces on the Western Front in 1918, and he accepted the armistice with Germany on 11 November 1918.

bio|03-20|1976|Τσέστερ Μπένινγκτον|Chester Bennington|Chester Bennington was an American singer, the lead vocalist of Linkin Park. The band became famous with the album "Hybrid Theory". He took his own life in 2017.

bio|03-20|1984|Φερνάντο Τόρρες|Fernando Torres|Fernando Torres is a former Spanish footballer. He played for Atletico Madrid, Liverpool and Chelsea, and won the World Cup of 2010 and the European Championships of 2008 and 2012 with Spain.

bio|03-20|1990|Λεβ Γιασίν|Lev Yashin|Lev Yashin was a Soviet goalkeeper for Dynamo Moscow. He is regarded as one of the greatest goalkeepers in history and was the only goalkeeper to win the Ballon d'Or, in 1963.

bio|03-20|1993|Πόλυκαρπ Κους|Polykarp Kusch|Polykarp Kusch was a German-American physicist. He measured the magnetic moment of the electron with great precision, and in 1955 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Willis Lamb.

bio|03-21|1556|Τόμας Κράνμερ|Thomas Cranmer|Thomas Cranmer was archbishop of Canterbury under Henry VIII. He helped the Reformation in England and wrote the "Book of Common Prayer". Under Mary I he was burned at the stake in 1556.

bio|03-21|1762|Νικολά Λουί ντε Λακάιγ|Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille|Nicolas-Louis de Lacaille was a French astronomer. He observed the southern sky from the Cape of Good Hope and recorded thousands of stars. He named 14 new constellations.

bio|03-21|1768|Ζοζέφ Φουριέ|Joseph Fourier|Joseph Fourier was a French mathematician and physicist. He developed the Fourier series and the Fourier transform, which analyse complex signals into simple sine waves, and he studied the conduction of heat.

bio|03-21|1910|Ναντάρ|Nadar|Nadar, whose real name was Gaspard-Felix Tournachon, was a French photographer and caricaturist. He photographed many famous people of Paris and took the first aerial photographs from a balloon.

bio|03-21|1936|Αλεξάντρ Γκλαζουνόφ|Alexander Glazunov|Alexander Glazunov was a Russian composer and conductor. He wrote symphonies and the ballet "The Seasons". He was director of the St Petersburg Conservatory and a teacher of Shostakovich.

bio|03-21|1958|Γκάρι Όλντμαν|Gary Oldman|Gary Oldman is an English actor. He won the Best Actor Oscar for his performance as Winston Churchill in "Darkest Hour". He also played in "Dracula" and in "Harry Potter".
bio|03-21|1960|Άιρτον Σένα|Ayrton Senna|Ayrton Senna was a Brazilian Formula One driver. He won three world championships with McLaren. He was killed in an accident at the Imola Grand Prix in 1994.

bio|03-21|1980|Ροναλντίνιο|Ronaldinho|Ronaldinho is a former Brazilian footballer. He played for Barcelona and Milan, and won the World Cup of 2002 and the Ballon d'Or in 2005. He was known for his dribbling and his smile.
bio|03-21|1991|Αντουάν Γκριεζμάν|Antoine Griezmann|Antoine Griezmann is a French footballer. He played for Atletico Madrid and Barcelona, and with France he won the World Cup in 2018.

bio|03-22|1459|Μαξιμιλιανός Α΄|Maximilian I|Maximilian I was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire from 1508. He belonged to the House of Habsburg and, through marriages and alliances, strengthened the influence of his family. He was succeeded by his grandson Charles V.

bio|03-22|1599|Άντονι βαν Ντάικ|Anthony van Dyck|Anthony van Dyck was a Flemish Baroque painter. He became known for his portraits and became court painter to Charles I of England. He was a pupil of Rubens.

bio|03-22|1687|Ζαν Μπατίστ Λυλί|Jean-Baptiste Lully|Jean-Baptiste Lully was born in Florence and became a composer at the court of Louis XIV of France. He created the French form of opera and worked with Moliere. He died of gangrene.
bio|03-22|1797|Γουλιέλμος Α΄|William I|William I was king of Prussia from 1861 and the first emperor of a united Germany from 1871. With his chancellor Bismarck he led the unification of the country.

bio|03-22|1832|Γιόχαν Βόλφγκανγκ Γκαίτε|Johann Wolfgang von Goethe|Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was a German writer and scientist. He wrote "Faust", "The Sorrows of Young Werther" and the "West-Eastern Divan". He was a minister in Weimar and died there.

bio|03-22|1868|Ρόμπερτ Άντριους Μίλικαν|Robert Andrews Millikan|Robert Millikan was an American physicist. He measured the charge of the electron with the oil-drop experiment, and in 1923 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|03-22|1976|Ρις Γουίδερσπουν|Reese Witherspoon|Reese Witherspoon is an American actress and producer. She became known for the film "Legally Blonde" and won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Walk the Line".

bio|03-22|2001|Σαμπιχά Γκιοκτσέν|Sabiha Gokcen|Sabiha Gokcen was a Turkish pilot and the adopted daughter of Kemal Ataturk. She was one of the first women military aviators in the world. She died in 2001.

bio|03-22|2005|Κένζο Τάνγκε|Kenzo Tange|Kenzo Tange was a Japanese architect. He designed the Hiroshima Peace Memorial and the Olympic venues in Tokyo for the 1964 Games. In 1987 he received the Pritzker Prize.
bio|03-23|1555|Ιούλιος Γ΄|Julius III|Julius III was pope from 1550 to 1555. He was mild and supported the Council of Trent. He did not have great success in reforming the Church.

bio|03-23|1749|Πιερ-Σιμόν Λαπλάς|Pierre-Simon Laplace|Pierre-Simon Laplace was a French mathematician and astronomer. He wrote "Celestial Mechanics" and contributed to the theory of probability. He was Minister of the Interior under Napoleon.
bio|03-23|1842|Σταντάλ|Stendhal|Stendhal, whose real name was Henri Beyle, was a French writer. He wrote "The Red and the Black" and "The Charterhouse of Parma". He died in Paris in 1842.

bio|03-23|1900|Έριχ Φρομ|Erich Fromm|Erich Fromm was born in Frankfurt and became a psychologist and philosopher. He wrote "The Fear of Freedom" and "The Art of Loving". After the Nazis came to power he emigrated to the United States.

bio|03-23|1904|Τζόαν Κρόφορντ|Joan Crawford|Joan Crawford was an American actress and a Hollywood star for decades. She won the Oscar for Best Actress for "Mildred Pierce" in 1946. She also starred in "What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?".
bio|03-23|1910|Ακίρα Κουροσάβα|Akira Kurosawa|Akira Kurosawa was a Japanese film director. He directed "Rashomon", "Seven Samurai" and "Ran". His cinema influenced many directors around the world.

bio|03-23|1912|Βέρνερ φον Μπράουν|Wernher von Braun|Wernher von Braun was a German engineer. He developed the V-2 rockets for Germany, and after the war he worked in the United States for NASA, where he led the development of the Saturn V rocket.

bio|03-23|1992|Φρίντριχ Χάγιεκ|Friedrich Hayek|Friedrich Hayek was an Austrian economist and philosopher. He wrote "The Road to Serfdom" and supported a liberal economy. In 1974 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Economics.

bio|03-23|2011|Ελίζαμπεθ Τέιλορ|Elizabeth Taylor|Elizabeth Taylor died in 2011. She was a British-American actress who won two Oscars, for "Butterfield 8" and "Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?". She was also an activist in the fight against AIDS.

bio|03-24|809|Χαρούν αλ Ρασίντ|Harun al-Rashid|Harun al-Rashid died in 809 in Tus. He was the fifth Abbasid caliph, and his reign is regarded as the golden age of Baghdad. He fought against Byzantium.

bio|03-24|1603|Ελισάβετ Α΄|Elizabeth I|Elizabeth I was queen of England from 1558 to 1603. Her era, the "Elizabethan" age, was a period of cultural flourishing with Shakespeare. In 1588 England defeated the Spanish Armada. She never married.

bio|03-24|1733|Τζόζεφ Πρίστλυ|Joseph Priestley|Joseph Priestley was an English theologian and chemist. He discovered oxygen in 1774, independently of Scheele, and other gases. Because of his political views he emigrated to the United States.

bio|03-24|1834|Γουίλιαμ Μόρις|William Morris|William Morris was an English designer, poet and socialist. He was the leader of the Arts and Crafts movement, which championed craftsmanship. He designed tapestries and fabrics with plant patterns.

bio|03-24|1874|Χάρρυ Χουντίνι|Harry Houdini|Harry Houdini was born in Budapest and grew up in the United States. He was a magician and an expert in escapes from handcuffs, locked boxes and bound situations. He became famous worldwide.

bio|03-24|1905|Ιούλιος Βερν|Jules Verne|Jules Verne died in Amiens in 1905. He was a French writer and a pioneer of science fiction, with works such as "Around the World in Eighty Days" and "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea".

bio|03-24|1926|Ντάριο Φο|Dario Fo|Dario Fo was an Italian playwright, actor and director. He wrote the play "Accidental Death of an Anarchist", and in 1997 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-24|1930|Στηβ ΜακΚουήν|Steve McQueen|Steve McQueen was an American actor. He became known for films such as "The Magnificent Seven", "The Great Escape" and "Bullitt". He was regarded as "the king of cool".

bio|03-24|2016|Γιόχαν Κρόιφ|Johan Cruyff|Johan Cruyff was a Dutch footballer and coach. He was the central figure of "total football" at Ajax and in the Dutch national team, and he played for Barcelona both as a player and as a coach.
bio|03-25|1223|Αλφόνσος Β΄|Afonso II|Afonso II was king of Portugal from 1211 to 1223. He carried out administrative and legal reforms and fought the Moors. He was the third king of Portugal.

bio|03-25|1767|Ζοακίμ Μυρά|Joachim Murat|Joachim Murat was a French marshal and the brother-in-law of Napoleon. He became king of Naples in 1808. After Napoleon's fall he tried to regain the throne and was executed in 1815.

bio|03-25|1801|Νοβάλις|Novalis|Novalis, whose real name was Georg von Hardenberg, was a German poet of early Romanticism. He wrote the "Hymns to the Night" and the unfinished novel "Heinrich von Ofterdingen". He died young, at the age of 28.

bio|03-25|1881|Μπέλα Μπάρτοκ|Bela Bartok|Bela Bartok was a Hungarian composer and pianist. He collected and studied Hungarian and Eastern European folk music and incorporated it into his works, such as the "Concerto for Orchestra".

bio|03-25|1914|Φρεντερίκ Μιστράλ|Frederic Mistral|Frederic Mistral was a French poet from Provence. He wrote in the Provencal language and led its revival. In 1904 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-25|1918|Κλωντ Ντεμπυσί|Claude Debussy|Claude Debussy was a French composer and one of the leading representatives of Impressionism in music. He wrote "Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun", "La Mer" and "Clair de lune". He died in Paris in 1918.

bio|03-25|1942|Αρίθα Φράνκλιν|Aretha Franklin|Aretha Franklin was an American singer. She is regarded as the "Queen of Soul", with hits such as "Respect" and "Think". She was the first woman to be inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

bio|03-25|1947|Έλτον Τζον|Elton John|Elton John is an English singer, pianist and composer. With Bernie Taupin he wrote songs such as "Your Song" and "Candle in the Wind". He also wrote the music for "The Lion King".

bio|03-25|1972|Ναφτάλι Μπένετ|Naftali Bennett|Naftali Bennett is an Israeli politician and former high-tech entrepreneur. He was prime minister of Israel from June 2021 to June 2022, in a coalition of parties.

bio|03-26|1827|Λούντβιχ βαν Μπετόβεν|Ludwig van Beethoven|Ludwig van Beethoven died in Vienna in 1827. He was a German composer who wrote nine symphonies, concertos, piano sonatas and an opera. He became deaf but continued to compose.

bio|03-26|1874|Ρόμπερτ Φροστ|Robert Frost|Robert Frost was an American poet. He wrote about the countryside of New England, with poems such as "The Road Not Taken". He won the Pulitzer Prize for Poetry four times.

bio|03-26|1892|Ουώλτ Ουίτμαν|Walt Whitman|Walt Whitman was an American poet and journalist. He wrote the collection "Leaves of Grass", with free verse and hymns to democracy and the human body. He is regarded as one of the greatest American poets.

bio|03-26|1911|Τενεσί Ουίλιαμς|Tennessee Williams|Tennessee Williams was born in Mississippi. He was an American playwright and wrote "The Glass Menagerie" and "A Streetcar Named Desire". He won two Pulitzer Prizes.

bio|03-26|1923|Σαρά Μπερνάρ|Sarah Bernhardt|Sarah Bernhardt was a French actress and was regarded as the greatest actress of the theatre of her time. She played roles such as Phaedra and Hamlet and toured the whole world.

bio|03-26|1941|Ρίτσαρντ Ντόκινς|Richard Dawkins|Richard Dawkins is a British biologist and writer. He wrote "The Selfish Gene" and introduced the term "meme". He is known for his views in favour of evolution and against religion.
bio|03-26|1973|Λάρρυ Πέιτζ|Larry Page|Larry Page is an American computer scientist. Together with Sergey Brin he founded Google in 1998 and developed the PageRank algorithm for ranking web pages.

bio|03-26|1985|Κίρα Νάιτλι|Keira Knightley|Keira Knightley is an English actress. She became known for the films "Pirates of the Caribbean" and "Pride and Prejudice", and she was nominated for an Oscar for "Pride and Prejudice" and for "The Imitation Game".

bio|03-26|2015|Τούμας Τράνστρεμερ|Tomas Transtromer|Tomas Transtromer was a Swedish poet and psychologist. His poetry is short and full of images of nature. In 2011 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.

bio|03-27|1845|Βίλχελμ Ρέντγκεν|Wilhelm Rontgen|Wilhelm Rontgen was born in Germany and was a physicist. In 1895 he discovered X-rays, and in 1901 he became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|03-27|1955|Μαριάνο Ραχόι|Mariano Rajoy|Mariano Rajoy is a Spanish politician of the People's Party. He was prime minister of Spain from 2011 to 2018, when he lost a vote of no confidence after a corruption scandal.

bio|03-27|1963|Κουέντιν Ταραντίνο|Quentin Tarantino|Quentin Tarantino is an American director and screenwriter. He directed "Reservoir Dogs", "Pulp Fiction" and "Kill Bill", and he won Oscars for Best Original Screenplay for "Pulp Fiction" and "Django Unchained".
bio|03-27|1968|Γιούρι Γκαγκάριν|Yuri Gagarin|Yuri Gagarin died on 27 March 1968 in a training flight with a MiG-15 aircraft near Moscow. He was the first human to travel into space, in 1961.
